answer: Each identity registers a dune station, locks an 80-credit bond, mounts a copper-wired mirror panel, and files a tilt-resistance log per epoch. Auditors recompute tilt and copper resistance from sun-angle and temperature tables; a log off by over 2% burns the bond. A fake station needs a keeper: first 34 credits, kth 34+7(k-1), 1000th 7027, so 1000 fakes cost 3,530,500 plus 80,000 bonds. A rented-mirror ring fails since one panel cannot file tilt logs for many stations in a window without duplicating a reading. An honest operator attends once, paying only its refundable bond.
